hook.text: Five companies control what most humans see, read, and share online. They weren't elected. They built products.

buildup.text: Network effects make social platforms natural monopolies. Your friends are on Facebook, so you join Facebook.

discovery.text: When a platform reaches critical mass, competition becomes nearly impossible. Switching means leaving your network.

twist.text: These monopolies aren't like Standard Oil. They give products away free. Traditional antitrust law doesn't fit.

climax.text: The EU, U.S., and China are all trying different regulatory models. None has solved the problem yet.

punchline.text: Free products can still cost you your choices.

quiz.question: Why are social media platforms considered natural monopolies?
